blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practice, and propagate religion to all individuals.
Article 26 protects collective religious rights, allowing religious denominations to manage their own internal religious affairs.
Article 27 prohibits the State from compelling any person to pay taxes meant specifically for promoting or maintaining any particular religion.
Article 28 provides rules regarding religious instruction in educational institutions based on their funding and administrative structure.
The right to 'propagate' under Article 25 does not include the right to forcibly convert another person to one's own religion.
Article 25 guarantees individual religious rights, whereas Article 26 guarantees rights to religious denominations or sections thereof.
Article 27 bans the levy of taxes for religious promotion, but it does not prohibit the levy of a fee to provide secular services or regulation.
Educational institutions wholly maintained out of State funds cannot impart any religious instruction under Article 28.
